newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: ACCC coy on Australia regional bank policy.
newsitem.headline: ACCC coy on Australia regional bank policy.

text.p: Anti-monopolies authority, the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCC), said on Tuesday it had not made a decision on whether to retain its policy on keeping one independent regional bank in each state.

The ACCC is currently assessing Westpac Banking Corp's takeover offer for Bank of Melbourne Ltd, which if it gives approval to, would effectively remove the last major independent regional bank in Victoria.
"I would never say definitely yes before a decision," ACCC chairman Allan Fels told reporters after a luncheon speech to the Committee for Economic Development of Australia (CEDA).
"So a regulator never says never and they never say defintely yes before they make a decision," Fels said.
The ACCC's one regional bank per state policy was formed after Westpac's takeover of Challenge Bank in 1995.
Fels said the commission would keep this policy unless there was persuasive evidence to the contrary then it wouldn't oppose a takeover of a regional bank.
